chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Salma ibn al-Khattab from Muhammad ibn Musa from Muhammad ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Walid from his father from his mother Umm Is'haq bint Sulayman

She said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) looked at me while I was breastfeeding one of my sons, Muhammad or Is'haq. He said: 'O Umm Is'haq! Do not breastfeed him from one breast, but breastfeed him from both of them, so that one becomes food and the other a drink.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended method for breastfeeding an infant according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises Umm Is'haq to alternate breastfeeding from both breasts, a practical instruction highlighting the importance of balanced nutrition for the infant. This guidance reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on applying prophetic wisdom to daily health practices, ensuring the child receives equal sustenance and hydration from each breast. The narration underscores the holistic approach to child-rearing in Shia tradition, where physical well-being is intertwined with spiritual and familial care.
